rules.text: 1 | Responsibility: Network Planning team identifies the Space required to setup Electrical Infra (CSS or DSS) for Project. Electrical Infra Building ( CSS/DSS) can be either Open to Sky of Part of Building. CSS space is upto 60 Sq.M wheras DSS Space varies from 200 to 800 Sq.m CSS - Consumer Substation DSS - Distribution Substation
2 | Responsibility: BD team communicates the space requirement to Developer
3 | Responsibility: Developer earmark tentative space and share the Autocad Project Plan / Layout to AEML
4 | Responsibility: Check - Tentative space earmarked in Autocad Layout is Open to Sky | Automation: Check - Tentative space earmarked in Autocad Layout is part of the Building

5 | Responsibility: Finalise the CSS/DSS Space Diamensions a. Plot Validated againest Muncipal Corporation DP Plan b. RG Complaince in case Plot is part of RG c. Mandatory Plot Clerances i. Boundary ii. DP road iii. Internal road iv. Nalla v. Maintenance space ( Front Door) vi. Nearby Structure vii.Trees viii. Any provisions in DP | Automation: Finalise the CSS/DSS Space Diamensions a. Check other infra beneth space earmarked i. Building Basement ii. Mother earth b. Mark developer building Column & Beams to check available space & Height
6 | Responsibility: Finalise CSS/DSS Space Access a. Wayleave - Doors to Building b. Cable Trench / Tray - Cable entry / Exit & Route in Plot d. Earth Pit Locations - Earthing strip Route
7 | Responsibility: Identify Footprint available for Equipments ( Floorwise in case of multiple Floors)
8 | Responsibility: Finalise Equipments to be installed ( Input from Network Planning team)
9 | Responsibility: Prepare Floorwise Equipment layouts considering Equipment Diamensions & Mandatory Clerances required ( refer separate excel for Equipment footprint & mandatory clerances required)
10 | Responsibility: Finalise Ventilations for Building
11 | Responsibility: Share the Electrical Infra ( CSS/ DSS) Building layout Autocad file to BD Team
11 | Responsibility: Share converged Equipment placement layout with Developer or ask for more space

12 | Responsibility: Prepare Autocad Layouts 1. Equipment layouts with Eathing ( Top View) 2. Platform Layouts ( Top View) 3. Building Cutout Layout ( Top View) 4. Cable Tray / Trench Layout ( Top View) 5. Sectional Layout ( Side & Front View)

rules.title: Retrieve before generating
rules.text: Retrieval runs first. Generation, validation and optimisation run only when no retrieved design clears the match threshold.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Return at least 3 matches
rules.text: The system returns at least 3 matches with a similarity score; above the threshold they go to the developer for use and adaptation.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Filter by known attributes
rules.text: Known attributes narrow the search first, e.g. an open-sky substation is matched only against open-sky sites.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Encode the site
rules.text: The proposed plot is converted into a data structure so shape and size similarity can be computed against historic plots.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Generate block by block
rules.text: When nothing clears the threshold, the layout is generated one block at a time; each block's output is summarised and passed to the next.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Validate against compliance
rules.text: Once all blocks are generated, the intermediate output is checked against the compliance requirements.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Optimise with clearance constraints
rules.text: If any check fails, optimisation routines with clearance constraints adjust the layout to reach the best compliant result.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Deliver 3 compliant options
rules.text: The process repeats until 3 compliant layout options are obtained.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Convert to 2D CAD
rules.text: Intermediate layouts are produced in a CAD-compatible structure and converted to 2D CAD files using Python CAD packages.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Approach overview / Steps 2–5

rules.title: Electrical configuration and equipment
rules.text: Transformer ratings, busbar arrangement, number of feeders, switchgear type, fault levels; equipment dimensions, weight, connection orientation, operating clearances.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Step 1 table

rules.title: Site constraints
rules.text: Available area, plot shape, building footprint, floor level, indoor/outdoor (open-sky) installation, centralised or distributed installation, standalone building or inside an existing building, whether on a platform.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Step 1 table

rules.title: Civil and structural
rules.text: Plinths, floor loading, cable trenches, equipment supports, substation height, beams/columns.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Step 1 table

rules.title: Cable routing and connectivity
rules.text: Cable entry/exit points, trench paths, cable capacity, equipment interconnections.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Step 1 table

rules.title: Access and ventilation
rules.text: Access paths, ventilation arrangement.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Step 1 table

rules.title: Objectives
rules.text: Speed up the design process; standardise substation layouts. Most substations are built from a small set of electrical configurations, so find a similar past design first and adapt it.
rules.source: Automated Substation Design Approach Note › Problem and objectives

rules.title: Transformer spacing
rules.text: AEML lists 750 mm on every side of a DT. Two adjacent DTs therefore need 1.5 m between them, which matches NBC cl. 4.2.1(17) at 11 kV. The Sadguru tentative layout (05.10.2026) shows about 1.0 m between DT2 and DT3, so it fails this rule unless a fire wall is added.

rules.title: Transformers above ground
rules.text: NBC allows oil-filled transformers only on G or B1. An upper-floor substation (as in the Sadguru layout) is defensible only under the flood provision, with written concurrence of AEML, the Electrical Inspector and the fire service.

rules.title: Shared ELV/HT duct
rules.text: NBC cl. 4.2.1(14) requires a dedicated HT shaft. A combined “ELV & HT” duct needs to be split.

rules.title: Draw-out breakers
rules.text: The LT ICOG front clearance grows with ACB rating (1.0 m to 1.7 m). Use the same logic for any panel with draw-out units.

rules.title: Gaps in the AEML rule sheet
rules.text: No clearances are given for the LTPCC 7W panel; customised substations have no weights; 100–450 kVAr capacitor clearances are blank.
